newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads tighten.

text.p: Light buying of conventional pass-throughs failed to lift U.S. mortgage-backed securities out of the doldrums on Wednesday, but yield spreads tightened modestly to Treasuries, mortgage experts said.
Mortgage banking activity increased after several sluggish days, giving a slight boost to volume in today's session, one trader said.
By late afternoon, pass-throughs were flat to 3/32 lower in most coupons while comparable Treasuries were 1/32 to 4/32 lower.

"Mortgages are doing (well)," said one trader at a large investment house in New York. He said he saw some buying of conventional 8.5 percent coupons versus five-year Treasuries. But conventional 8.5 percents ended down one tick on the day.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 2/32 at 99-26/32, yielding 95 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was 2/32 lower as well, at 99-27/32 and 100-01/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 3/32 to 6.60 percent.
